descs.8079: A large crowd of civilians files into your ship, some even filling the cargo holds, as soon as your ship touches down.  Their leader reminds you that they are expected at <RST> by <DL>.
descs.8080: Civilians quickly scramble into your ship, filling your living spaces and some of your more comfortable cargo holds.  Their leader reminds you that they are expected at <RST> by <DL>.
descs.8092: As you bring your ship to a halt on the landing grounds, a wiry man approaches you and says under his breath, “Good to see you, finally.  I’ll wait on your ship while you visit the station.  You are safe for the moment, but don’t dally.  The Rebels will catch up with us soon enough.”
descs.8093: A rotund, unkempt individual approaches you as you arrive in the landing area.  “Rrrm...  I see yer havin’ some data I should be lookin’ at.  Thank ye...  I’ll send ye me findins before yer leavin’ this port.”
descs.8102: The Rebel spy screams as soon as she’s on board, “Get me back to Palshife... FAST!!!”
descs.8104: You find and sneak the scientist past the Ruby security forces. “No time for small talk,” the scientist says. “Get me the hell out of here, and I’ll tell you anything you want to know.”
descs.8105: “GO! GO! GO!,” the SEAL commander screams. “We’ve got the data, now get us the hell out of here!”
descs.8106: You land on the planet and trasmit the coded message given to you on Palshife with your current coordinates. After several hours, you hear a knock on the hull. “Boy, are we glad to see you,” the SEAL commander says. “We only had about a week’s worth of supplies and oxygen left. It seems I owe you my life this time, Captain. We got the data. Get us back to Palshife.”
descs.8107: Your boarding party quickly recovers the prototype weapon and returns to stow the device in your hold.
descs.8109: As you land a ragged looking woman approaches you. She hands you a single plastic card with a gold chip embedded in it. “Keep it safe...” is all she says as she walks on by and fades into the mass of people in this gritty docking area.
descs.8110: As you board the ship everyone is glad to see you.  You yell out asking if there are any friends of Lucas on board.  A young man fights through the throng of people and presents himself to you. “I have important information for Lucas.  You have to get me to him immediately.” The two of you board the <PSN>, ignoring the rest of the passengers and crew.
descs.8111: As Joseph leaves your ship he gives you new directions: “My father has traveled to <RST> and is meeting with Rebel leaders to try to secure help against the pirates. Proceed there and meet him - he will give you your payment. In the meantime, I will talk to the Hunters."
descs.8112: As Lucas leaves your ship he says, “Thank you for the lift, my friend. Please go to <RST> and tell my son that all is nearly ready. If the militias and Rebels won’t help, then perhaps I will find another here who will.”
descs.9005: You activate the core-drilling rig and extract <CQ> tons of core samples from the crust of <DST>.
descs.9107: “Unfortunately, you destroyed the weapon, Captain,” the Rebel officer says, shaking his head. “However, at least the ’Feds didn’t get it. Without the weapon, we can’t pay you, though. Thank you for all your assistance.”
descs.10002: The sign above the door to this spaceport cantina is made of a piece of the heatshield of a 21st-century reentry vehicle. It reads “The Aerobrake.”
descs.10004: Welcome to The Bunker - the most heavily shielded bar in the Sol system!
descs.10005: Welcome to the Levo Bar & Grill - home of the best plastiburgers this side of the Gamma Quadrant!
descs.10006: The sign on the window of the spaceport bar advertises “Real, Old-Fashioned Guinesses.”
descs.10008: Welcome to The Sandblast, Dune’s local spacebort tavern.
descs.10009: The sign outside the door reads “Welcome to Cloud Nine.”
descs.10010: Welcome to The Max - Gamorrean Starbursts are only 5 credits on Thursdays!
descs.10012: Welcome to the Northstar bar & grill.
descs.10016: Welcome to Pat’s Airlock - Home of the finest chips in the galaxy.
descs.10019: This bar is called The Flatlands. Somehow, you don’t find yourself wondering why.
descs.10021: Welcome to The Refinery - We specialize in petroleum, deuterium, and alcohol, of course!
descs.10022: Ironically, the bar in New Sahara’s spaceport is named Ocean Breeze.
descs.10023: Welcome to The Drop Zone. Care to try our 2-for-1 special on synthobeer?
descs.10024: If this tavern is any indication, you can plainly see that while Plateau may be flat, it certainly isn’t boring. Sights and sounds from across the galaxy assault your senses from all directions.
descs.10028: This is your average spaceport bar - dark and dingy, but with the touch of class that comes with serving the pilots of ships that travel to the stars.
descs.10031: This is surely an unremarkable tavern for a planet that’s practically covered with them.
descs.10032: The floors of the Sandstorm Bar & Grill have been polished smooth by the abrasive sand that spacers track in from outside, on the landing pads.
descs.10033: At the Palshife Spaceport Bar, it’s a tradition to raise a glass to friends and aquaintances who have died in combat with the Confederation tyrants.
descs.10035: This spaceport bar is mounted near the top of the air-traffic control tower, providing a spectacular view of the spaceport and the countryside beyond.
descs.10036: The walls of this bar are fairly covered with the residue of all the tall tales that have been told in here.
descs.10037: The bartender at the Zaxted Pub will serve you any drink you want, as long as it’s not synthetic.
descs.10039: This is just another unremarkable bar, on an unremarkable planet. The only thing that’s different is the logo on the napkins. That, and the pretzels are slightly saltier here.
descs.10043: The proprietor, a war veteran, has covered the walls of this bar with old news printouts from the Great War.
descs.10045: The slightly inebriated customers of this spaceport pub invite you in to play Caber Tag... “A real man’s game!”
descs.10046: The Pot O’ Gold Tavern is covered with pictures of Old Ireland.
descs.10048: Diphidia’s spaceport bar is decorated in a maritime theme, reflecting the planet’s heavy emphasis on ocean-based industry and trade.
descs.10049: This bar is festooned with mountain-climbing paraphernalia; rock-climbing is a popular sport among the cliffs of New Columbia.
descs.10053: This bar is perplexingly decorated with examples of primitive computer technology, though you can’t fathom the reason why.
descs.10055: The Blackthorne Cantina is generally not a good place to bring the kids.
descs.10059: This hole-in-the-wall of a bar is where the bored and tired crewmembers who work for the refinery come after a long shift in the fluid processing facility.
descs.10060: Welcome to the Ursa Minor Bar. Our drink of the day is the Samarium Cobalt Sunset.
descs.10062: The miners and engineers of the Pegasus colony often come here to the Unicorn Tavern to relax after a long shift.
descs.10063: This is a lonely bar on a lonely world. The bartender is glad for the company: the few people who do stop in here each day usually would rather be in a spaceport bar in a more exciting star system... anywhere but Sauron.
descs.10064: The Total Eclipse Bar is, surprisingly, extremely bright inside. You wonder if the powerful halogen lighting in the establishment is a subconscious response to the pervasive darkness outside.
descs.10065: This pub is the spaceport’s premier authentic-German beverage-vending establishment.
descs.10068: The Jayock Tavern is decorated with pictures of strange, mythical creatures from many different planets.
descs.10071: The sign outside originally read “Murphy Spaceport Bar,” but some wag has changed it to read “The School Of Hard Knocks.”
descs.10075:
Welcome to the Tree Hugger Juice Bar. Today’s special is fresh-squeezed alfalfa juice, produced by union labor and poured into
non-polluting handcrafted earthenware mugs.
descs.10079: The Buzzbird Bar is a great place to relax, what with all the humming peepers they keep in cages all over the barroom. The employees of the bar wear special earplugs to keep from being lulled into peaceful catatonia while on the job.
descs.10080: The entire 10-meter length of this bar is covered with the hide of a single Banderfrog. Your admire the designers for picking such a durable material with which to decorate this establishment; however, you question their choice of colors.
descs.10081: The spaceport bar on Sirgil III is very quiet... all the action seems to be taking place up in orbit at the Sirgil Starport.
descs.10082: This bar is packed with people. Apparently, business is booming for the shopowners and entrepreneurs of Sirgil Starport, because people from all over the galaxy come here to trade their wares.
descs.10084: This is just another unremarkable spaceport bar, much like all the others you’ve seen in your travels. However, they do seem to mix an especially good vodka and plinkberry juice here.
descs.10085: The dimly lit “Bottom O’ The Bucket” is filled with starborne mercenaries and other remnants of the Lethe-Cydonia war. The bartender looks nervously at you, always keeping one eye on the entrance.
descs.10086: The holovid in the corner of the Lethe spaceport bar is perpetually tuned to one of the Lethe news services, so that the patrons can keep up to date on the progress of the war.
descs.10090: The Eyepatch Tavern is definitely not a place you want to insult drunken pirates in. Or sober ones, for that matter.
descs.10093: The spaceport bar on Ruby is frequented by scientists, engineers, and technicians from the various research facilities housed in nearby structures.
descs.10097: Each member of the insipid band that is attempting to entertain the drunken patrons of this bar seems to be playing his part in a different key from everyone else.
descs.10101: Ah, the Evildrome Boozarama. Built out of the remains of a crashed freighter, this bar is frequented by some of the roughest characters in the galaxy. A starship captain can be shot on sight just for parking his ship on some pirate’s favorite landing pad.
descs.10105: The guy at the next table looks so nasty that you wouldn’t be surprised if he had a wooden leg and an eyepatch. As you glance about uneasily, you become aware of how easy it would be for you to have your throat slit in this place.
